Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — thanks + follow-ups

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated properly: 

Recap of requirements we heard on the call:
- Primary workload: multi-turn chat for customer support triage + long-form summarization for tickets.
- Expected traffic: steady-state ~30 TPS, peak bursts up to ~120 TPS (5-6 minute bursts around product launches).
- Typical token mix: input ~150 tokens, output ~300 tokens on average (~450 tokens total / request).
- Concurrency: roughly 40-70 concurrent sessions during peaks (users keep sessions open for context).
- Model preference: you mentioned wanting a 70B chat model (internal candidate) with quantized weights if possible.
- Latency target: <400ms p50 for short responses; streaming acceptable for long outputs.
- Compliance: currently OK with Redwood Dedicated (not immediate on VPC/private), but will evaluate Private later for audit controls.

Questions we still need from your infra team (if you can share):
1) Any hard SLOs (p99) we should size for?
2) Typical prompt length variance (any workloads with >2k tokens)?
3) Is batching acceptable for your application flow? (we can tune to reduce unit costs)

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa will put together a preliminary Dedicated sizing recommendation (GPU SKUs + instance counts + expected throughput).
- We'll share a short cost/throughput tradeoff matrix and an MOP we can iterate on.
- Schedule a tech deep-dive next week to review perf numbers and confirm model/quantization approach.

Attachments: ava_infra_metrics.png (your perf dashboard screenshot), ava_mau_forecast.xlsx (you shared on the call).

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa on the sizing doc.

Best,
Rafael

Thanks Rafael — that looks accurate. A couple clarifications from infra/pm: 

- SLOs: p50 <350ms, p95 <800ms, p99 ideally <1.5s (we're flexible on p99 during rare bursts).
- Long requests: ~5% of requests can exceed 2k tokens (ticket dumps / full-ticket summarization).
- Batching: okay for background summarization jobs; for chat we prefer lower added latency — but small batches (2-4) are acceptable if p95 is still met.

GPU question: our infra lead asked whether Redwood Dedicated typically recommends H100 vs A100 for this profile and what the rough capacity difference would be for a 70B model. Also can you include a low/medium/high sizing option and the expected TPS/concurrency for each?

We'd like a 30-minute tech deep-dive with your performance engineer next week — Tue or Wed mornings PT work best.

Sara Lee

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — proposal draft

Rafael / FYI — initial sizing draft attached. High-level recommendations based on the numbers Sara provided:

Assumptions used:
- Model: 70B chat-family (float16 baseline, with option for 4-bit quantized inference).
- Token mix: 450 tokens/request average; 5% >2k tokens handled as outliers.
- Latency targets: p50 350ms, p95 800ms.
- Batching: conservative batching for chat (avg batch 1.6), heavier batching for async summarization.

Sizing options (ballpark):
- Low (cost-first): 4x A100-80GB -> ~peak 60-80 TPS sustained, concurrency headroom ~30-40. Good if you can accept slightly higher p95 during bursts.
- Medium (balanced): 4x H100 -> ~peak 120-150 TPS with better batching efficiency, concurrency ~60-80. Meets p95 targets for your median workloads.
- High (performance/headroom): 6x H100 -> ~200+ TPS peak, concurrency 120+, handles >2k token requests with less impact on latency.

Notes / tradeoffs:
- H100 gives materially better throughput on large models and when leveraging FlashAttention + optimized kernels; A100 still economical for steady, lower-TPS workloads.
- Quantization to 4-bit reduces memory & increases throughput but needs evaluation on quality/regression tests. We can run a quick eval against your prompt set.
- KV cache + prefix caching will reduce cost for repeat conversational context — we should instrument a small prod trace to estimate cache hit rate.

Cost ballpark: we included monthly committed-dedicated estimates in the attached PDF (redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm which sizing tier you want us to prototype (we can spin a Medium tier PoC within 5 business days).
2) Schedule a 30–45m performance deep-dive (I'll join with an infra engineer). Tue/Wed mornings PT slots noted.
3) Share a small prompt/sample set (10–20 prompts) so we can run quality/regressions on quantized variants.

I attached the sizing PDF and included a short table of expected TPS by model variant. Let me know which day works for the deep-dive and I’ll send a calendar invite.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
